panel.label: Squeeze
panel.name: ss_squeeze
panel.text: Keeps textures compressed on the graphics card, saving video memory.

button.name: ss_squeeze_help
button.tool_tip: Roughly a quarter of the video memory for the same picture. Click for how it works, and when it falls back to the ordinary path.

check_box.label: Use GPU-compressed textures
check_box.name: ss_squeeze_enabled
check_box.tool_tip: Needs a graphics card supporting BC7, which means roughly anything from 2012 onward. Cards without it fall back to the normal texture path automatically.

check_box.label: Build compressed textures in the background
check_box.name: ss_squeeze_background
check_box.tool_tip: Uses spare processor cores while you are logged in, at low priority. Turning this off means only textures already compressed on disk are used.

check_box.label: Finish downloading textures so they can be compressed
check_box.name: ss_squeeze_network
check_box.tool_tip: Compression only happens at full resolution, because a compressed copy of a blurry texture would be thrown away as soon as you walked closer. Partly downloaded textures are quietly completed while you are idle.

slider.label: Share of the cache for compressed textures (%):
slider.name: SSSqueezeCachePercent
slider.tool_tip: A share of the total cache size set in the Network and Cache tab, not extra disk on top of it. The rest goes to the ordinary texture cache, which stays the source these are rebuilt from. Compressed textures are a fixed size per pixel while the originals are heavily compressed, so half the bytes is nowhere near half the textures. Least recently used are dropped only as the limit is approached.

slider.label: Processor cores to use (0 = automatic):
slider.name: SSSqueezeEncodeThreads
slider.tool_tip: Compression runs at low priority so it should stay out of the way of the viewer itself. Lower this if you notice other programs slowing down.
